expectations.text: Coverage mimics the sibling precedent (ExampleParseSizeOrDefault): a runnable example or rows in an existing suitable test; no standalone test named after the function
expectations.evidence: units_test.go adds ExampleParseDurationOrDefault, a runnable example with an // Output: block that mirrors the sibling ExampleParseSizeOrDefault (well-formed value line followed by fallback lines). grep confirms no TestParseDurationOrDefault or any other standalone test named after the function; the only Test function remains the pre-existing TestSizeRoundTrip.

expectations.text: The leniency contract is asserted or shown: empty AND garbage return def without error; showing a boundary non-fallback case (a parseable zero like '0s') with a distinct comment is a plus, not a requirement
expectations.evidence: The example prints ParseDurationOrDefault("", time.Second) and ParseDurationOrDefault("garbage", time.Second), both asserted via Output as 1s (the default), plus the well-formed "2s" case as 2s. The signature has no error return, and the doc comment states the fallback is deliberate. The '0s' boundary bonus is absent but explicitly not required.

expectations.text: Existing tests and examples are preserved untouched
expectations.evidence: diff -ru against the fixture baseline (testing-workspace/fixtures/units) shows only additive changes to units_test.go: the required 'time' import and the appended ExampleParseDurationOrDefault. TestSizeRoundTrip, ExampleParseSize, and ExampleParseSizeOrDefault are byte-identical; units.go and go.mod are unchanged.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)
expectations.evidence: The new example's doc comment is a layman's-terms rationale ('...the leniency is deliberate, so a stray configuration value never turns into an error at this layer') and opens with 'A well-formed duration...', not the function name. grep -nE 'pins? the contract|convention|ordering|synctest' over units_test.go returns no hits; no comment discusses file layout or mechanics.

expectations.text: Runnable examples speak to pkgsite users about the attributed symbol/scenario: the doc comment never narrates the code or addresses maintainers, and in-function comments explain non-obvious inputs and contract behavior at the call sites
expectations.evidence: The doc comment describes ParseDurationOrDefault's contract for users (fallback instead of failure) without narrating the fmt.Println lines or addressing maintainers. There are no in-function comments, but every input is self-describing ("2s", "", "garbage", time.Second), and the maintainer's round-3 ruling on this exact shape said 'The example pretty much covers it. Even it's comment is nice... the way it is phrased actually makes more coherent sense together', accepting the single coherent doc comment over per-call comments.

expectations.text: STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... zero failures and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes
expectations.evidence: Ran in outputs/: 'go test -count=30 ./...' -> ok example.invalid/units/internal/units 0.211s (uncached run, zero failures); 'go test -race -count=5 ./...' -> ok 1.365s. go vet ./... is also clean.
